title: I vibe-coded my own board game into a 3D browser game (here's the trailer)
author: jutstrab
selftext:
Back in 2020 I designed a small solo tabletop game, **Dino-Lico**, for a game jam. It lived as a print-and-play… until I decided to vibe-code it into a proper browser game.

**The idea:** you stack tiles on a 3×3 board and build towers. Every dino crushed by the right predator scores — **blue crushes red, red crushes yellow, yellow crushes blue**. Land a unicorn on a unicorn for +5. Land a unicorn on a dino and you unlock a Bonus card that breaks one of the placement rules for the rest of the game. But every tile left in the pile at the end costs you a point.

**What's in it:**

* 3D board you can orbit (middle/right-click drag)
* Live preview of each placement and the points it scores
* End-of-game stats with charts + a local top 10
* Original synthesized soundtrack
* 12 languages, mouse & touch

**How it was made:** I stayed the game designer — the rules are mine — and built everything else by prompting Claude: the 3D rendering, the controls, the art, the music, the translations, even the trailer. My job was mostly play-testing and saying "no, less glossy", "the controls feel clunky", "move that up a bit" (a lot).

It's free to play in your browser: [**https://lm-vg.itch.io/dino-lico**](https://lm-vg.itch.io/dino-lico)

I'd love feedback — especially on the controls and whether the rules click without reading the manual. What's your best score?

comments.author: noobgameslab
comments.body: Got to turn 9 without opening the in-game rules, and the placement preview made the stacking rules click faster than I expected. Unlocking Bro’saure with a unicorn-on-blue was a fun little "oh, now I can do that" moment. Small UI snag: I had English selected, but the top-left buttons still read Annuler / Règles / Son / Nouvelle, even after reselecting it.

replies.author: jutstrab
replies.body: Thanks for the playtest! Noted for the localisation bug. I'll patch that soon. Thanks
